title: Augmenting regulatory T cell stability and function in systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjogren’s disease with TYK2 inhibitors
summary:
In patients with autoimmune diseases, there is an imbalance in the immune system: On the one hand, inflammatory cells are overactive for no known reason. On the other hand, anti-inflammatory cells are not active enough. These cells, which are supposed to prevent unnecessary inflammation in the body, are called 'regulatory T cells'. Most medications used to treat autoimmune diseases suppress the overactive inflammation, leading to an improvement in symptoms. These medications, however, often also suppress the regulatory T cells.
Since 2023, a medication called deucravacitinib (Sotyktu®) is available, inhibiting inflammatory pathways in immune cells. Currently studies investigating this medication in systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren’s disease are ongoing. We assume that this medication not only suppresses the overactive inflammatory cells of the immune system but also activates the protective regulatory cells.
This study aims to determine whether the medication actually activates regulatory T cells and thereby restores balance of the immune system.
To examine this, we would like to treat these cells with the medication in the laboratory and examine them.
conditions: Systemic lupus erythematosus with organ or system involvement

interventions.name: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus or Sjögren's disease having no or mild disease activity will have blood drawn once. The differentiation of these patients' regulatory T cells will be investigated in cell culture under inflammatory conditions and under TYK2 inhibition.

Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus or Sjögren's disease having moderate to high disease activity will have blood drawn once. The differentiation of these patients' regulatory T cells will be investigated in cell culture under inflammatory conditions and under TYK2 inhibition.

Patients without an acute or chronic inflammatory disease will have blood drawn once. The differentiation of these patients' regulatory T cells will be investigated in cell culture under inflammatory conditions and under TYK2 inhibition.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Diagnosed with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) according to the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR)/American College of Rheumatology (ACR) 2019 classification criteria for SLE
or
Confirmed diagnosis of SjD, either by satisfying the 2016 ACR/EULAR criteria for the classification as primary SjD or secondary SjD in association with a diagnosis of a secondary chronic disease
or
Absence of any chronic inflammatory or autoimmune disease in the personal medical history (immunologically healthy controls).
2. Approximately 50% of the subjects within the respective patient cohorts need to have a duration of disease ≤ 10 years before blood withdrawal.
3. Patients with a diagnosis of primary or secondary SjD need a positive anti-SSA-antibody test (according to local lab threshold value) at or within 6 months prior to blood sampling.
4. Indication for a blood withdrawal due to diagnostic or drug safety reasons, independent of study participation.
5. Evidence of a personally signed and dated informed consent document with assent as appropriate indicating that the subject has been informed of all pertinent aspects of the study.
Exclusion criteria:
SLE patients:
1. Diagnosis of drug-induced SLE rather than idiopathic SLE. SLE patients with secondary Sjogren’s syndrome are not excluded.
2. SLE overlap syndromes including, but not limited to, rheumatoid arthritis, scleroderma, and mixed connective tissue disease.
3. History of biopsy proven lupus nephritis.

Healthy Control patients:
1. Presence of a chronic inflammatory disease.

All participants (SLE patients, SjD patients, and healthy controls):
1. Age at study inclusion <18 years.
2. History of congenital or acquired immunodeficiency, other than SLE or SjD and its treatment.
3. Known active infection, or any major episode of infection requiring hospitalization or treatment with parenteral (intramuscular or IV) antimicrobial agents (eg, antibiotics antiviral, antifungal, or antiparasitic agents) within 4 weeks of blood withdrawal, or treatment with oral antimicrobial agents within 2 weeks of blood withdrawal.
4. History or current symptoms suggestive of any lymphoproliferative disorder, such as Epstein Barr Virus (EBV) related lymphoproliferative disorder, history of lymphoma, leukemia, or signs and symptoms suggestive of current lymphatic disease.
5. Corticosteroid therapy:
a) Oral corticosteroid therapy cannot exceed 20 mg/day in the 4 weeks preceding blood withdrawal.
b) Intramuscular or intravenous corticosteroid pulse therapy in the 4 weeks preceding blood withdrawal.
6. Any prior treatment with non B cell-specific lymphocyte depleting agents/therapies [eg, alemtuzumab, alkylating agents (eg, cyclophosphamide or chlorambucil), total lymphoid irradiation, etc]. Subjects who have received rituximab or other selective B lymphocyte depleting agents are eligible if they have not received such therapy for at least 1 year prior to blood withdrawal and have had normal CD19/20+ counts in the last flow cytometric analysis performed.
7. Use of one of the following drugs within 7 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to blood withdrawal:
a) JAK1/2/3 inhibitors (eg, Tofacitinib, Baricitinib, Upadacitinib, Filgotinib) or TYK2 inhibitors (eg, deucravacitinib)
b) Anifrolumab or other anti-type I-interferon receptor-antibodies.
c) Abatacept or other inhibitors of antigen presenting cell – T cell co-stimulation.
8. Vaccination within the 4 weeks preceding blood withdrawal.
9. Significant trauma or major surgery within the 4 weeks preceding blood withdrawal.
10. Severe allergic disease requiring medical attendance within the 4 weeks preceding blood withdrawal.
11. Subjects with a malignancy or with a history of malignancy with the exception of adequately treated or excised non-metastatic basal cell or squamous cell cancer of the skin or cervical carcinoma in situ.
12. Self-reported pregnant or nursing females are excluded.
13. Other severe acute or chronic medical or psychiatric condition or laboratory abnormality that may interfere with the interpretation of study results or, in the judgment of the investigator, would make the subject inappropriate for entry into this study.
